The '''Saint Petersburg Mathematical Society''' ({{langx|ru|Санкт-Петербургское математическое общество}}) is a [[scientific society|mathematical society]] run by [[Saint Petersburg]] [[mathematician]]s.

==Historical notes==
The St. Petersburg Mathematical Society was founded in 1890 and was the third founded mathematical society in Russia after those of [[Moscow Mathematical Society|Moscow]] (1867) and [[Kharkov Mathematical Society|Khar'kov]] (1879).<ref name="webhistory">{{harv|Saint Petersburg Mathematical Society|2012}}.</ref><ref name="Vershik1993p21">{{harv|Vershik|1993|p=21}}.</ref> Its founder and first president was [[Vasily Imshenetskii]],<ref name="webhistory" /> who also had  founded earlier the Khar'kov Mathematical Society.<ref>According to {{Harvtxt|Ostrovskii|1999|p=26}}</ref>

The Society was dissolved and subsequently revived twice, each time changing its name, sometime in between 1905 and 1917, the society ceased to function and by 1917 it had completely dissolved, perhaps due to the social agitations that destroyed many existing Russian scientific institutions.<ref name="Vershik1993p21" />  It was re-established by the initiative of [[:ru:Васильев, Александр Васильевич (математик)|Alexander Vasilyev]] in 1921 as the Petrograd Physical and Mathematical Society (subsequently called the Leningrad Physical and Mathematical Society). In 1930, the self-dissolution of the society was due to political reasons.<ref>See {{harv|Lorentz|2002|loc=§4}} for an account of the events leading to its closure.</ref> Before the beginning of [[World War II]] in 1941, [[Leonid Kantorovich]] proposed to revive the society, and a similar failed attempt was made by [[Vladimir Smirnov (mathematician)|Vladimir Smirnov]] in 1953: only in 1959 [[Yuri Linnik]] did succeed in reestablishing the society (then called the Leningrad Mathematical Society).<ref>{{harv|Lorentz|2002|p=191}}.</ref> It regained the original name the ''St. Petersburg Mathematical Society'' in 1991.

==Activities==

==="Young mathematician" prize===
The "Young Mathematician" prize<ref>The laureates of the annual ''Young Mathematician'' prize
of the St. Petersburg Mathematical Society [http://www.mathsoc.spb.ru/mol_mat.html]</ref> has been awarded since 1962.
